verdict_reason: The estimator is a held-out stratified/grouped logistic-regression separability probe and it is exact: driving the same liblinear + class_weight='balanced' + StratifiedKFold(3, shuffle, seed 42) configuration by hand reproduces sklearn's cross_val_score(scoring='roc_auc') fold for fold to a maximum absolute difference of 0.0 ([0.979591836734694, 0.9047619047619048, 0.9047619047619047] both ways), and a planted linear concept returns mean AUC exactly 1.0. Both round-3 counterexamples are closed on the current code: the case that filters a layer down to 4+4 rows in only 2 groups now yields layer AUCs [0.38567649281934996, nan] instead of an uncaught GroupKFold ValueError, and the explicit 6/3/3-group case returns the controlled error 'No layer produced finite separability values' instead of a one-class LogisticRegression fit. I found 0 value-changing counterexamples on the binary-integer-label domain.
comparable_reason: AUC is dimensionless with chance 0.5, and it is invariant to rotation and to zero-padding of the representation, so the headline is structurally comparable. The caveat is that the probe is liblinear at a FIXED C = 1.0 with no standardisation, so it is not invariant to a positive rescaling of the activations even though linear separability is: on one fixed 40x16 problem the CV mean AUC moves 0.5158730 (scale 1e-3) -> 0.5374150 (1) -> 0.5572562 (100) -> 0.6048753 (1000), i.e. +17.2% for the same geometry. Residual-stream norms differ by orders of magnitude across families, so part of any cross-model AUC difference is regularisation strength rather than readability. On my 4-model panel mean_auc is 0.555619 (pythia-70m) / 0.649786 (pythia-160m) / 0.709404 (distilgpt2) / 0.712900 (gpt2), a plausible spread with no saturation.
github_reason: The released RepE code implements the PCA/LAT reading-vector pipeline (rep_reading_pipeline, PCARepReader / ClusterMeanRepReader) over the authors' own stimulus sets; it contains no held-out logistic-regression CV AUC estimator over a bundled fact-pair set, so there is nothing runnable to compare number-for-number. task_metadata.py:124 already declares this a refined adaptation in the paper's linear-reading family (Sec. 5.1) rather than a reimplementation. The runnable reference for the estimator itself is scikit-learn, and against cross_val_score the agreement is 0.0.
paper_reason: Zou et al. (arXiv:2310.01405) publishes PCA/LAT accuracies (e.g. 81.0 / 85.0 / 72.5 / 92.6 / 90.7 for Utility, Morality, Power, Probability, Risk) obtained with a different reader, different stimuli and different models; BLME reports gpt2 mean CV AUC 0.712900 on its own 39 minimal fact pairs. Model, stimuli, reader and statistic all differ, so no relative error is meaningful, and the BLME manuscript carries 0 concrete result rows for this task. There is no published number to reproduce.
confounds_reason: What the task measures is factual-knowledge readability on 39 bundled minimal pairs, so a capability signal is expected and is not a size artifact per se; on my 4-model panel mean_auc is 0.7129 (gpt2, 124M) and 0.7094 (distilgpt2, 82M) against 0.5556 (pythia-70m, 70M) and 0.6498 (pythia-160m, 162M), i.e. it does NOT order with parameter count (gpt2 > pythia-160m despite fewer parameters), which is what a knowledge probe should look like. The suspicion is the scale channel above: a fixed-C penalty makes the AUC partly a function of activation norm, and residual norms grow with depth within a family, so depth can enter through the regulariser rather than through readability.
defects: ESTIMATOR, representation_engineering.py:625: LogisticRegression(solver='liblinear', ..., default C=1.0) with no standardisation is not scale-equivariant although linear separability is. Same data, pure positive rescaling: mean AUC 0.5158730 at 1e-3 vs 0.6048753 at 1e3 (+17.2%). Standardising per fold, or scaling C by 1/mean(||x||^2), would make the probe measure separability rather than separability-times-norm.

ESTIMAND/SCOPE, representation_engineering.py:344-383: the measurement is entirely determined by BLME's 39 bundled world-knowledge minimal pairs (capitals, boiling points, polygon sides, arithmetic). That is a documented adaptation, but it means 'concept separability' here is 'factual-knowledge linear readability on these 39 items', and a model that lacks the facts scores ~0.5 for reasons unrelated to representation engineering.

PROTOCOL, defaults.yaml:333-334 with num_samples = 20: `_reps = max(1, (20 + 38)//39) = 1`, so only the FIRST 20 of the 39 bundled fact pairs are used (40 rows) and 19 pairs never enter the probe. I replayed the union-find grouping: it yields 11 groups over those 20 pairs (sizes 2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,1,1), which is >= n_splits = 3, so GroupKFold IS used and all three materialised folds carry both classes -- the entity-swap leak is genuinely closed at the shipped config. But the realised group and fold counts are not emitted, so a reader cannot audit which CV produced the number.

NO UNCERTAINTY: mean_auc is a mean over 3 folds on 40 rows with no standard error emitted; at n=40 the fold-to-fold spread on my gpt2 run is material (per-layer AUCs span 0.5939-0.8016) and max_auc is an argmax over 12 correlated per-layer estimates, so `max_auc` is upward biased as a point estimate.

DOCS, representation_engineering.py grouping comment: it states the union-find 'yields 19 independent groups (largest 6)' over the 39 pairs; replaying the exact _vary/_STOP/union-find logic I get 17 groups, largest 6. The conclusion (far more groups than the 3 folds need) is unaffected.
